entities.summary: Richard Henry Lee was an American statesman and Founding Father from Virginia, best known for the June 1776 Lee Resolution, the motion in the Second Continental Congress calling for the colonies' independence from Great Britain leading to the United States Declaration of Independence, which he signed. Lee also served a one-year term as the president of the Continental Congress, proposed and was a signatory to the Continental Association, signed the Articles of Confederation, and was a United States senator from Virginia from 1789 to 1792, serving part of that time as the second president pro tempore of the upper house.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Richard Henry Lee's June 1776 Lee Resolution in the Second Continental Congress led to the United States Declaration of Independence, a foundational document that shaped the course of American and world history. His presidency of the Continental Congress and signing of key documents like the Articles of Confederation further solidified his influence on early American governance.
